sections.heading: Grados de certeza
sections.body: Debe (95%+): conclusión lógica a partir de la evidencia. Podría/puede/podría (30–60%): posibilidad, no segura. No puedo/no pude (cerca del 0%): imposibilidad lógica: contradice la evidencia.

sections.heading: Deducción pasada
sections.body: Agregue "tener + participio pasado" para deducir sobre el pasado: "Ella debe haberlo olvidado". "Es posible que ya se haya ido". "No puede haber sido ella; estaba en el extranjero".

examples.english: She must be exhausted — she's been awake for 30 hours.
He might be in a meeting.
That can't be right — I checked the figures myself.
She must have missed the train.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite each sentence using a modal verb of deduction (must, might, can't/couldn't) with the correct level of certainty.
items: I'm certain he is at home — his car is in the driveway. (present)
It's impossible that she finished already — she just started. (present)
I'm sure the package was delivered — here's the tracking confirmation. (past)
answers: He must be at home — his car is in the driveway.
She can't have finished already — she just started.
They might have / may have missed the train.
The package must have been delivered — here's the tracking confirmation.

quiz.question: "Ese no puede ser Tom; se mudó a Australia". 'No puedo' aquí expresa:
quiz.explanation: "No puede ser" expresa una imposibilidad lógica basada en evidencia, equivalente a "es imposible que sea Tom".
